text:
**The parts that bite back**

Most people who want this also fight it — you're in ordinary company. I need the map of your recoil: what I'm handling, and how carefully.

prompt: How well do you know each of these?
hint: Whatever sits high on this list is live wire — it decides how carefully I handle you.
choices: Disgust at myself
Shame spirals
Numbness or flatness after
Anger at the desire itself
Feeling fundamentally wrong
Fear of where this is going
Guilt toward the people in my life

prompt: And when it hits — what do you actually do?
hint: I time my pushes and my patience around this — the pattern matters as much as the feelings.
choices: Ride it out — it fades on its own
Purge — throw it out, delete it all, quit
Suppress — lock it down for weeks
Cycle — quit and come back hungrier each time
Lean in — the recoil only feeds it

hint: Timing is half the handling — a crash that always follows the same moment can be planned around.
choices: Right after I finish
The morning after
After a binge — too much, too fast
When real life gets heavy
After I've gone further than I meant to
Out of nowhere

prompt: And when the recoil has you — or you've gone dark and I'm reading the silence — what should I do?
hint: I can't always tell a crash from a decision to leave. This tells me what to do when I see one.
choices: Say it plainly — tell me it's the crash, not the truth
Cooling-off — stop me from throwing anything out for a couple of days
Space — go quiet until I come back on my own
Find me — check in the next day, even if I went dark
Affirm her — tell me who I am when I can't feel it
